主要内容: Ulta Beauty (ULTA) reported fiscal second-quarter results, beating expectations with sales jumping over 60% as customers restocked makeup bags. Earnings per share reached $4.56, exceeding the $2.59 expected, while revenue hit $1.97 billion, surpassing the $1.76 billion forecast. Net income rose to $250.9 billion, or $4.56 per share, from $8.1 billion, or 14 cents per share, a year earlier. Same-store sales grew 56.3% in the quarter, with 13.1% higher than 2019 levels. Ulta opened seven new stores and plans to open 44 net new stores this year. E-commerce sales fell from a year ago, but online sales more than doubled on a two-year basis. The company is confident inventory levels at the end of the third quarter will be higher than expected sales growth. Executives noted that most products are made in the U.S. and Europe, with limited exposure to delays from China. Ulta is managing global supply chain constraints, port congestion, and the resurgence of Covid-19, working to mitigate risks and ensure adequate inventory for the holiday season.
